R0.label: Frontier token revenue
R0.basis: Anthropic run-rate $65B at end-July 2026 (Bloomberg, 17 Aug 2026; the path ran $14B Feb → $30B Apr → $47B May → $65B Jul) with investors expecting $100–120B by year-end; OpenAI $40B (Bloomberg, 13 Aug 2026); Epoch puts the two at $105B combined, up 3.5× since January. Google does not break out Gemini API revenue; Z.ai, MiniMax, DeepSeek, xAI and Mistral add a few billion. Rounded sum entering Q3 2026.
R0.rule: R0 = R0_epoch + R0x, derived in one place
R0.short: Total frontier revenue run-rate = Epoch’s disclosed sum + the undisclosed allowance. Derived; edit the two parts.

sh_rd.label: AI R&D share
sh_rd.basis: The article’s own attribution (“all numbers are estimates”). Coding is probably larger: 44% of Anthropic API traffic is computer & mathematical work (Economic Index, Jan 2026), Claude Code alone was ~18% of Anthropic’s run-rate in February, programming is over half of OpenRouter traffic, and SemiAnalysis puts coding above 65% of lab ARR. Quant demand is real but unquantified (Jane Street weighing 100–200 MW; XTX above 25k GPUs). Lab-to-lab token buying has no public figure, though labs are the buyers behind Mercor’s ~$2B run-rate and Anthropic spends over $1B a year on RL environments.
sh_rd.short: Cattani’s attribution. Evidence says coding is larger (44% of Anthropic API traffic; Claude Code ~18% of its run-rate) and trading is undocumented.

sh_swe.label: Software engineering share
sh_swe.basis: Raised on OpenAI's first-party Enterprise Signals: Codex was 64% of combined Codex+ChatGPT enterprise output tokens in June 2026, alongside coding at 44% of Anthropic API traffic and SemiAnalysis's >65% of lab ARR; a token-share rather than revenue measure, so 20 stays well below the 'coding' scenario's 45. (reported, 2026-08-12). First-party OpenAI usage data (Enterprise Signals, updated 12 Aug 2026) puts agentic coding at 64% of combined Codex+ChatGPT enterprise output tokens as of June 2026, alongside the existing evidence base (coding 44% of Anthropic API traffic, SemiAnalysis >65% of lab ARR). The model still carries software engineering at 15%, well below every measured coding share. Move the full capped +5 to 20; the 'coding' scenario's 45 remains the upper case.
sh_swe.short: Raised on OpenAI's first-party Enterprise Signals: Codex was 64% of combined Codex+ChatGPT enterprise output tokens in June 2026, alongside coding at 44% of Anthropic API traffic and SemiAnalysis's >65% of lab ARR; a token-share rather than revenue measure, so 20 stays well below the 'coding' scenario's 45.

H0.label: 80% task horizon today
H0.basis: METR Time Horizon 1.1: Claude Mythos Preview 3h06m at 80% success (measured Mar 2026), o3 30 min. Fable 5 / Mythos 5 have no METR measurement yet. Horizons are human-expert task length; METR flags measurements above 16 h (50%) as unreliable.
H0.rule: latest state-of-the-art 80%-success time horizon in METR’s benchmark file, in hours
H0.short: Latest state-of-the-art 80%-success horizon in METR’s benchmark file (Claude Mythos Preview, measured March 2026).

D0.label: Horizon doubling time
D0.basis: METR TH1.1: 129 days for the 50% horizon since 2023; o3 → Mythos Preview implies ~4.4 months on the 80% horizon; the original 2025 paper found 7 months over 2019–2025. AI Futures revised its median to 4–4.5 months in April 2026.
D0.rule: METR’s since-2023 doubling time in days ÷ 30.4
D0.short: METR’s since-2023 doubling time for the task horizon, converted from days to months.

H_sat.label: Bounded demand saturates at
H_sat.basis: Chinese open-weight models passed 60% of OpenRouter tokens in July 2026 and the US share fell from 70% to 30% in a year; DeepSeek V4-Flash lists at $0.14/$0.28 per million tokens and OpenAI cut Luna 80% in July; fixed-capability prices fall 10× to 200× a year (a16z, Epoch). DeepSeek raised prices in August as its capacity filled, so migration saturates. Applies to bounded work only.
H_sat.short: Assumption: bounded tasks stop pulling demand once the horizon passes a working week.

subst.label: Migration to non-frontier models
subst.basis: Vercel AI Gateway (tens of trillions of production tokens/month): open-weight models ran 71.5% of gateway tokens and took 23% of spend in September 2026, up from 56% and 14% in August — direct production-traffic evidence of bounded work migrating off frontier endpoints, with frontier spend still growing in absolute terms. (estimate, 2026-10-15). Same series that set the current value: Vercel AI Gateway production index (tens of trillions of production tokens/month). September data: open weight 71.5% of tokens (vs 56% in August) and 23% of spend (vs 14%), a share of spend that 'has more than quadrupled since June'. The article also reports 'Since December, spend on frontier models has grown tenfold; spend on open-weight models has grown more than seventyfold' and that almost one in three teams switched their most-used lab in September, an index record - bounded work keeps leaving frontier
subst.short: Vercel AI Gateway (tens of trillions of production tokens/month): open-weight models ran 71.5% of gateway tokens and took 23% of spend in September 2026, up from 56% and 14% in August — direct production-traffic evidence of bounded work migrating off frontier endpoints, with frontier spend still growing in absolute terms.

K0.label: Frontier compute online today
K0.basis: Anthropic ~1.4 GW end-2025 heading to 3.7–5 GW by end-2026 (Epoch; analyst estimates); OpenAI above 2 GW end-2025 with ~1.5 GW of Stargate due in 2026; Patel has each of the two labs above 5 GW during 2026. No official total exists; frontier labs hold only 20–30% of global AI compute (Epoch, May 2026) but take a third of 2026 additions, rising to 70–80% by 2028 (Patel).
K0.rule: estimated GW of frontier-lab compute online, from lab disclosures and analyst estimates
K0.short: Analyst estimates: Anthropic 3.7–5 GW and OpenAI above 2 GW in 2026 (Epoch); Patel has each above 5 GW. No official total.

pipe.label: Committed pipeline, next 18 months
pipe.basis: Observed frontier revenue grew ~5.8× over the last four quarters (Epoch’s disclosed sum) while quarter zero sits at 100% utilisation, so capacity must be growing far faster than the earlier 16 GW pipeline implied. Analyst estimates put the labs near 26 GW by end-2027 (Epoch and others); Patel has the two big labs tripling to ~18 GW each. 24 GW over six quarters is the middle of that range. Calibrated 2026-09-03 on the maintainer’s instruction.
pipe.rule: GW contracted to come online within six quarters, from lab and cloud announcements
pipe.short: Calibrated to observed revenue growth under the compute-constrained stance: between Epoch-style analyst estimates (~26 GW by end-2027) and Patel’s tripling (~40 GW). Capacity arriving within six quarters.

lead.label: Build lead time
lead.basis: First-GW deliveries from Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom run 12–18 months from signing; the larger Stargate sites announced in 2025 complete in Q4 2028.
lead.short: First-GW deliveries run 12–18 months from signing; large Stargate sites take longer.

capexGW.label: Capex per GW
capexGW.basis: Nvidia management puts its own revenue opportunity per GW at $18B (Hopper), $25B (Blackwell) and $40B (Vera Rubin); adding shell, power and land, all-in capex per GW sits above the previous $45B estimate. (reported, 2026-08-26). Silicon-and-systems content alone is now $40B per GW under Vera Rubin (2.2x Hopper, 1.6x Blackwell). Adding building, power and land, all-in capex per GW must exceed the current $45B assumption; I move to the +20% per-run cap (54) rather than the $60B+ the arithmetic implies.
capexGW.short: Nvidia management puts its own revenue opportunity per GW at $18B (Hopper), $25B (Blackwell) and $40B (Vera Rubin); adding shell, power and land, all-in capex per GW sits above the previous $45B estimate.

mono.label: Revenue ceiling per inference GW
mono.basis: Was derived so that quarter zero sat at 100% utilisation; inverted on 2026-09-07 so utilisation is an output. Dylan Patel: ‘$15B a GW turned into $50B+ of revenue’ for Anthropic (Dwarkesh Podcast, 25 Aug 2026); Tomasz Tunguz: Anthropic ‘as high as $50M per megawatt’ (27 Aug 2026), both on a total-compute basis, so higher per inference GW; SemiAnalysis models ~$100B/GW/yr of inference revenue potential (Aug 2026); the frontier fleet as a whole earns far less per GW. $50B per inference GW is a middle reading; moves under the revenue_per_gw rule, ±10% per run.
mono.short: Revenue potential per GW of inference capacity at current prices. Evidence-driven: Patel and Tunguz put Anthropic near $50M per MW of total compute (higher per inference GW); SemiAnalysis sees ~$100B/GW potential; the industry average is far lower.

train.label: Compute used for training
train.basis: Anthropic 2025: $4.1B training vs ~$2.7B inference (Epoch, Feb 2026), matching the 60/40 rumour the article cites. Amodei’s stylised split is 50/50; older forecasts have training falling toward 20% by end-2027.
train.short: Anthropic 2025 spent $4.1B on training vs ~$2.7B on inference (Epoch); Patel’s 60/40 split.

targetUtil.label: Utilisation labs build toward
targetUtil.basis: Debt’s share of hyperscaler capex rose from 9% (FY2024) to 32% by mid-2026 (FactSet); Morgan Stanley expects 52% of 2025–28 data-centre capex to be externally financed. Builds scale with the market index and fall with rates.
targetUtil.short: Assumption: labs build toward 80% utilisation of monetisable capacity.

buildMax.label: Max build pace
buildMax.basis: Debt’s share of hyperscaler capex rose from 9% (FY2024) to 32% by mid-2026 (FactSet); Morgan Stanley expects 52% of 2025–28 data-centre capex to be externally financed. Builds scale with the market index and fall with rates.
buildMax.short: Labs can add up to a quarter of their fleet per quarter (~2.4× a year), between analyst pace and Patel’s tripling.

fin.label: Financing sensitivity to markets
fin.basis: Datacentres are financed like real estate at 70%+ debt, with ~$4T of AI infrastructure issuance estimated over five years (Tunguz, Sep 2026); builds scale with credit and market conditions. (estimate, 2026-09-04). New quantitative sizing of the debt dependence of the buildout: $4T of issuance over five years, equal to 143% of the entire global private credit market and 286% of US commercial paper, with data centres financed as real-estate projects at 70%+ debt. That is a materially larger debt share than the FactSet 9%->32% figure the current value rests on, so builds should scale more, not less, with credit and market conditions. Modest move within the per-run limit (1 -> 1.3) rather than to the credit-scenario level of 2.
fin.short: Datacentres are financed like real estate at 70%+ debt, with ~$4T of AI infrastructure issuance estimated over five years (Tunguz, Sep 2026); builds scale with credit and market conditions.

r_sens.basis: Modelling constant; see “How the model works”.

rate0.label: Neutral rate
rate0.basis: Neutral rate = trailing-365-day mean of the effective Fed funds rate + 0.4 term premium. Budgets and builds respond to rates relative to this level, so a realised hike bites until the average catches up.
rate0.short: The policy rate the last year’s plans were made at: trailing-year mean of Fed funds + 0.4 term premium. Refreshed daily from FRED.

overhang.label: overhang
overhang.basis: Modelling constant; see “How the model works”.
overhang.short: Latent demand may exceed monetisable capacity by up to this fraction; the excess is served at scarcity prices.

R0x.label: Undisclosed frontier revenue (est.)
R0x.basis: Google does not break out Gemini API revenue, and Meta, Microsoft and Amazon run frontier-class inference internally; none appears in Epoch’s disclosed run-rates. Azeem Azhar puts generative-AI revenue above a $175B run-rate in June 2026 against ~$105B disclosed by the two big labs at the time, so an allowance of roughly $10B is a conservative reading. Estimate; the researcher may move it with sourced evidence.
R0x.short: Allowance for frontier revenue outside Epoch’s disclosed set (Gemini API, hyperscaler-native inference). Estimate, moved only with sourced evidence.
R0x.rule: analyst or company evidence on undisclosed frontier revenue

H_cap.label: Horizon ceiling
H_cap.basis: METR flags horizon measurements above 16 hours as unreliable, and past a few work-years the metric stops meaning anything. The ceiling slows the doubling as horizons approach it, so capability progress and the demand it pulls fade instead of compounding without limit. Assumption; the pipeline never moves it.
H_cap.short: Doubling slows as the horizon approaches this length; assumption, never moved by the pipeline.

R0_epoch.label: Disclosed frontier revenue (Epoch)
R0_epoch.basis: Sum of the latest full-company annualised run-rates in Epoch’s revenue dataset for the frontier labs it tracks.
R0_epoch.short: Epoch’s disclosed sum; the collector rewrites it daily. Total revenue = this + the undisclosed allowance.

orgX.label: Organic growth multiplier
orgX.basis: Scales the organic (non-reflexive, non-capability) growth of every segment. Calibration handle: the pipeline compares trailing observed revenue growth with the model’s quarter-zero growth and may move this under the growth_calibration rule when the gap persists.
orgX.short: Scales organic growth in every segment; the calibration handle for observed vs modelled growth.

scarce.label: Scarcity pricing
scarce.basis: When demand outruns capacity, revenue per GW rises with the excess: revenue = capacity × (1 + 0.5 × ln(utilisation)). Encodes Dwarkesh’s point that compute gets pricier when supply binds, and lets demand shocks show in revenue while rationed. Assumption.
scarce.short: Revenue per GW rises with excess demand when supply binds.

mSmooth.label: Budget response speed
mSmooth.basis: Token budgets and build decisions respond to a smoothed market index (40% adjustment per quarter), not to the index the same quarter. Matches 2026: a 29% semiconductor drawdown produced no budget or capex response, while sustained conditions do. Assumption.
mSmooth.short: Budgets follow a smoothed market index; dips pass, sustained moves bite.

rateGap.label: Rates vs neutral
rateGap.basis: Where policy stands relative to the neutral rate today: effective Fed funds + 0.4 − neutral. The FOMC raised the target range by a quarter point on 16 Sep 2026 (12–0), the first hike of the cycle; the gap turns positive as that prints in the effective rate and narrows again as the trailing average catches up.
rateGap.short: Today’s policy rate (+0.4) minus the neutral rate. A realised hike widens it; the model’s markets and build financing respond to it.

scenarios.name: Cattani base case
scenarios.who: Giovanni Cattani (@giovannicatt3)
scenarios.thesis: About half of frontier inference revenue comes from three unbounded, long-horizon tasks: AI R&D (~20%), software engineering (~15%) and trading (~15%). Their spend feeds their own revenue and funding, so growth is real but partly self-fuelled, and a single trigger could unwind up to half of it.

scenarios.name: Compute gets 10× pricier
scenarios.who: Dwarkesh Patel; Gavin Baker (Atreides)
scenarios.when: essay 29 Jul 2026; podcast with Dylan Patel 25 Aug 2026
scenarios.thesis: Lab revenue is growing ~10× a year against compute growing ~3×, so unless margins reach the mid-90s the price of compute has to rise 10–15×. Anthropic exits 2026 at $100–150B and the trend points to $1T a year later; Patel sees revenue per MW going from ~$50M to $70–80M by end-2027, and Baker a shortage through 2028. Modelled as high loop gains, strong contagion, labs building as fast as physics allows, and revenue per GW stepping up 50% in 2027 and again in 2028. His premise that labs are compute-constrained today (“double the compute, double the revenue”) is held as the inputs move.

anchors.note: Dwarkesh: the trend points to ~$1T a year after Anthropic exits 2026 at $100–150B

scenarios.name: Takeoff
scenarios.who: AI Futures Project (“AI 2027”)
scenarios.thesis: METR’s doubling time revised from 5.5 to 4–4.5 months, an “automated coder” arriving between late 2027 and early 2030 with ~$500B of lab revenue at that point, and lab revenue growing 5–7× a year in the meantime; growth turns superexponential only near the finish. Modelled as a 4-month doubling, a strong R&D feedback on progress, a breakthrough at end-2027, and labs building ahead of demand.

anchors.note: AI Futures: lab revenue growing 5–7× a year before the automated-coder point

scenarios.name: Capex supercycle
scenarios.who: Hyperscaler Q2 2026 calls; Morgan Stanley, UBS, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs
scenarios.thesis: Microsoft: “demand continues to exceed available supply”; Amazon: not enough capacity in 2026 or 2027; Nvidia has supply for ~70% of demand. Contracted backlog tops $2.4T across Microsoft, Oracle, Google, AWS and CoreWeave, and the banks see capex of $0.8–1.0T in 2026 rising to $1.2–1.6T a year by 2028 ($5.5T through 2030 at JPMorgan). Modelled as a bigger committed pipeline and labs building toward 65% utilisation rather than 80%. The premise that demand already exceeds supply is held as the inputs move.

scenarios.name: Enterprise wave
scenarios.who: Adoption data: Ramp AI Index, McKinsey State of AI, Stripe
scenarios.thesis: 55.7% of US businesses now pay for AI (Ramp), 40% of $1B+ companies are scaling agents (McKinsey) and Stripe’s top-100 AI firms grew revenue 175% year-to-date, with Cursor going from $1B to $2B in three months. Nvidia frames an agent as 15–100× a human’s compute. The next leg comes from everyone else, which also makes demand less fragile. Modelled as an eight-quarter adoption wave from 2027, a little reflexivity in the “everything else” bucket, slower migration to cheap models, and hyperscalers building for backlog.

scenarios.name: Coding is the market
scenarios.who: SemiAnalysis; Anthropic Economic Index; Ramp
scenarios.thesis: Coding is 44% of Anthropic API traffic and, by SemiAnalysis’s estimate, more than 65% of lab ARR; Anthropic is now paid for by 43.5% of US firms on Ramp. That is far above the article’s 15% software share, and it means the loop runs mostly through software startups. Modelled as a 45% software share with a higher software loop gain and a small trading share.

scenarios.name: Rate shock 2027
scenarios.who: Macro bears; Dallas Fed; Cattani’s own trigger list
scenarios.thesis: The backdrop is already tight: the Fed held at 3.50–3.75% in July with three hawkish dissents, markets price ~70% odds of a September hike, the 10-year is at 4.79%, CPI is 3.4% and oil is up 41% on the year. Higher rates slow the debt-financed buildout and drain the procyclical budgets at once, and the Dallas Fed notes ~$300B of AI bond issuance in 2026 adds an eighth of Treasury supply in duration, a second-round feedback. Modelled as a persistent shock: two points on rates for eight quarters from Q1 2027.

scenarios.name: Sharp correction 2028
scenarios.who: 2026’s own pattern: the June–July semiconductor selloff
scenarios.thesis: The SOX fell 29% from its June record on a Broadcom guidance miss, yields and tariff talk, then rebounded double digits in August; 71% of fund managers expect no hyperscaler capex cut. Modelled as a single −30% valuation shock in early 2028 with nothing else changed, which shows the model’s asymmetry: one-off shocks bounce, persistent ones cascade.

scenarios.name: Demand bubble bursts
scenarios.who: Ed Zitron; Andrew Ho (ex-OpenAI)
scenarios.thesis: OpenAI and Anthropic are 73–75% of AWS’s AI revenue through 2028 and ~70% of Microsoft’s and Azure’s; non-lab AI compute demand is under $30B against more than $1T of capex, so “if either dies, 40–73% of AI compute demand evaporates”. Ho adds that cheap distilled models force a Red Queen’s race in which lab revenue never catches spend. Modelled as near-total contagion and high procyclicality, then a 2028 funding stumble: a −30% market shock, labs cutting R&D tokens 40%, startups and quant desks cutting 30%, and 30% of the pipeline cancelled.

scenarios.name: Revenue gap
scenarios.who: David Cahn (Sequoia), Bain, Jim Covello (Goldman Sachs); Gartner; MIT NANDA
scenarios.when: Jul 2026; Sep 2025; Jun 2026; revised 14 Oct 2026 (Gartner impairment forecast)
scenarios.thesis: Cahn's $600B question is now a multi-trillion question. Gartner (14 Oct 2026) puts the arithmetic plainly: AI data centre owners need $8.5T of cumulative revenue through 2030 to cover announced capex, financing costs and a 12% ROIC, while total enterprise and consumer AI revenue reaches only $3.6T, leaving over $3.5T of spending exposed to impairment and forcing more than 80% of neocloud providers to stop operating independently. Bain still needs $2T by 2030 and sees an $800B shortfall; Covello doubts the use cases ever justify the spend. Demand grows, but nothing like fast enough to service the capital stack.

scenarios.name: Scaling wall
scenarios.who: Capability sceptics (Gary Marcus et al.)
scenarios.thesis: Progress slows to a ten-month doubling and R&D spend stops buying speed. Without new capability, unbounded demand loses its pull and bounded work migrates to cheap models.

scenarios.name: Price collapse
scenarios.who: Commoditisation bears; Tomasz Tunguz (Theory Ventures)
scenarios.when: Apr 2026 - Oct 2026, revised 13 Oct 2026 ('Price War in the Chip Aisle')
scenarios.thesis: Token prices keep falling faster than volume compensates. Five frontier models are within five points of each other on intelligence while cost per task spans 3.8x; Google's Argon prices at $1.99 a task, 74% below the dearest model, and Microsoft's Maia 300 and OpenAI's Jalapeno put custom silicon into inference. With intelligence per watt doubling every six months, Tunguz expects pricing to keep deflating at 40-70% margins - a second leg of cuts after the September Opus repricing, while Ramp records flat token spend on rising volumes.

scenarios.name: Credit event
scenarios.who: Michael Burry, Jim Chanos, IMF, Moody's, Epoch AI; SemiAnalysis on financing and on Nvidia's off-balance-sheet obligations
scenarios.thesis: Capex overtook hyperscaler operating cash flow in Q3 2026 (Epoch), so the marginal dollar is borrowed: $225B of hyperscaler bonds by mid-2026, $1.2T of lease commitments of which $820B have not started. SemiAnalysis now adds the vendor-credit leg: Nvidia disclosed $530B of gross off-balance-sheet guarantees in its latest 10-Q, up from $184B the prior quarter, against ~$450B of expected EBITDA, and ~$7T of AI-related debt is due by 2029, underwritten against GPU depreciation curves that are no longer falling. A credit repricing hits builds and valuations together.

scenarios.name: Consensus middle
scenarios.who: Epoch AI; Azeem Azhar; Benedict Evans; Ben Thompson
scenarios.thesis: Revenue is outgrowing compute (the two big labs went from $30B to $105B of run-rate between January and August against chip stock growing ~3.3× a year; tokens ~10× a year against inference capacity 3.4×), so utilisation stays above 90% and growth converges to the pace of capacity: roughly $200–300B by end-2027 and $350–600B in 2028. Real revenue that only just clears depreciation, with Oracle and CoreWeave spreads as the early-warning gauge. Modelled as slightly lower loop gains, capacity already 95% used today (the view’s own premise, held as the inputs move), and labs building at up to 22% of the fleet a quarter toward 90% utilisation.

anchors.note: Epoch: the two big labs at $200–300B by end-2027, scaled to the frontier total
Epoch: $350–600B in 2028, scaled to the frontier total

scenarios.name: Physics sets the pace
scenarios.who: Dylan Patel / SemiAnalysis
scenarios.thesis: Neither cash nor demand binds; N3 wafers, HBM, EUV tools, turbines and transformers do. The two big labs still roughly triple capacity a year (over 5 GW each in 2026, ~18 GW each by end-2027) and take 70–80% of incremental compute by 2028; ecosystem capex runs ~$11T over 2024–29, $6T cash and $5T debt; one-year H100 rentals are up 40% and on-demand capacity is sold out. Modelled as a bigger pipeline, builds capped near tripling, six-quarter lead times, and revenue per GW stepping up 40% in 2027 as labs outpay for compute. The camp’s premise that capacity is fully used today is held as the inputs move.

scenarios.name: Grid bottleneck
scenarios.who: SemiAnalysis (Maya Barkin, Reyk Knuhtsen, Jeremie Eliahou Ontiveros, Dylan Patel) grid, behind-the-meter, moratorium and Texas permitting analyses
scenarios.when: Jun-Jul 2026; revised 15 Sep 2026; revised 24 Oct 2026 (Texas TCEQ freeze audit)
scenarios.thesis: Firm power, turbines and transformers set the pace — and permitting politics now bite as well. September's parcel-level audit of 300+ moratoriums found only ~2.3 GW genuinely delayed because behind-the-meter generation was the workaround; Governor Abbott's 21 Sep directive closes it, telling TCEQ to stop issuing any datacenter-linked permit until ERCOT finishes its review. SemiAnalysis's site-by-site audit finds six Texas campuses, 8.7 GW in all, needing air permits during the pause; three already have a first tranche of generation permitted, one has filed and two have not. Base case: TCEQ resumes in December after ERCOT's 10 Dec report, the phases needing permits soon slip about a quarter and the rest of the forecast holds. Build pace stays capped near 0.18 a quarter with a six-quarter lead, and revenue per GW stays tied to realised utilisation.

scenarios.name: No reflexivity
scenarios.who: Control case
scenarios.thesis: Every loop gain at zero: what demand looks like if token spend never fed back into revenue and funding. The gap to the base case is the reflexive share.
scenarios.retired_reason: Control case, not a market view; the reflexive-share tile reports the same number. Retired to respect the 16-scenario cap.

scenarios.name: AI factory economics — dollars per gigawatt
scenarios.who: Jensen Huang and Colette Kress, Nvidia Q2 FY2027 earnings call
scenarios.thesis: Nvidia's revenue opportunity per gigawatt has climbed from ~$18B (Hopper) to $25B (Blackwell) to $40B (Vera Rubin); top-five hyperscaler capex is heading for ~$800B in 2026 and $1.3T in 2027; supply stays the bottleneck through fiscal 2028 with ~70% supply-constrained growth guidance. Capital spending therefore grows much faster than physical gigawatts: each GW costs ~$60B all-in, the fleet grows slower than the dollars suggest, and the price of compute rises. The call’s premise that supply is the bottleneck today is held as the inputs move.
scenarios.retired_reason: Retired to make room for “Self-improvement loop too weak”: the least distinct structural scenario (closest path to its neighbours, 15%).

scenarios.name: Concentrated customer base
scenarios.who: Ara Kharazian, Ramp Economics Lab
scenarios.when: 14 Oct 2026 (Ramp AI Index, 'Cracks in the AI Thesis Part 3'); concentration data 2 Sep 2026
scenarios.thesis: 80% of OpenAI and Anthropic enterprise revenue comes from 1% of customers, and that top 1% is itself tech and AI firms. The October index shows that cohort stalling: $9,568 per employee per month in September, 3.1% below the July high of $9,873, two straight months of virtually no growth in token spend even as volumes rose, overall adoption at 55.9% and decelerating (top of the S-curve), and enterprise contracts negotiated on the customer's terms. A concentrated, already-flat buyer base cuts together when markets turn.

scenarios.name: Elasticity beats price decline
scenarios.who: Citadel Securities Global Macro Strategy
scenarios.when: Aug 2026 ('Elastic Expectations'; follows the June 'Tokenomics' note)
scenarios.thesis: Usage-weighted token prices have fallen 40% since end-June, yet July AI spend per employee among the top 1% of enterprises rose about 50% month over month, GPU rentals stayed above their June lows and Q2 hyperscaler cloud revenue shows incremental capacity finding paying demand fast. Cheaper intelligence expands the quantity consumed rather than shrinking the ecosystem's revenue, so the revenues embedded in today's expectations can be met by volume rather than price.
scenarios.retired_reason: Retired to make room for “Swarms buy speed, not intelligence”: the least distinct structural scenario (closest path to its neighbours, 19%).

scenarios.name: Agent swarms buy speed
scenarios.who: Noam Brown (OpenAI) with Dwarkesh Patel, Dwarkesh Podcast
scenarios.thesis: Parallel agent swarms turn latency into a purchasable good: OpenAI's Millennium-problem run used 10,000 agents and 130 billion tokens over 88 hours, and in GPT-5.6's Ultra Mode four agents halve wall-clock time for 2x the tokens, 16 agents continuing sublinearly. Token spend per task therefore rises with willingness to pay for speed even between model releases, so demand responds strongly to capability and lab R&D becomes the most token-hungry segment.

scenarios.name: Self-improvement loop too weak
scenarios.who: Ramez Naam (guest post on Noah Smith's Noahpinion)
scenarios.thesis: AI already helps improve AI, but on measured data the self-improvement loop is roughly 5–10x too weak to sustain itself, let alone run away: no signs of runaway acceleration, sharp diminishing returns to more tokens and experiments, and exponentially more resources needed just to hold the current pace. Progress stays fast by the standards of any other technology, so demand keeps growing, but R&D compute spend buys little extra speed and there is no intelligence-explosion kink.
scenarios.retired_reason: Retired to make room for “Capacity overhang”: the least distinct structural scenario (closest path to its neighbours, 13%).

scenarios.name: Capacity overhang
scenarios.who: Jason Li, Epoch AI
scenarios.thesis: Chips shipped through 2027 could run 30-170 million concurrent frontier-model agents (~1.9 billion on efficient open models like DeepSeek V4 Pro); Codex agent-hours cost $16-18 and Claude Code $24-50 at API prices. Using just 20% of that capacity implies $2.6-5.3T a year of API-equivalent spending, against roughly $1T of model-developer revenue by end-2027 even at fivefold annual growth. Demand grows fast but supply grows faster: utilisation, not revenue, is what breaks.

scenarios.name: Swarms buy speed, not intelligence
scenarios.who: Ramez Naam (futurist), cross-posted on Noahpinion by Noah Smith
scenarios.thesis: Parallel agents are an input with steep diminishing returns: more agents buy speed, not intelligence. Observed multi-agent scaling curves fall orders of magnitude short of RSI-model assumptions (Chan/Hinton/Bengio assume doubling effective research labour raises the software improvement rate ~2.6x), and OpenAI spent 124x the tokens per researcher for only 1.6x the experiments per researcher. Naam's calibration puts the measured software feedback loop five to ten times below self-sustaining. Token burn in AI R&D stays enormous while the feedback from that spend into capability and revenue is weak, and extra R&D spend buys little extra speed.
